You may follow him at Twitter @FidelRahmati Photo:The London headquarters of MI6, which was established in 1909 – Spotmatik Britain’s MI6 has been ranked as Europe’s most powerful intelligence service in a new survey of current and former intelligence officials, with France’s Directorate-General for External Security (DGSE) in second place and the Netherlands’ intelligence service taking third. The ranking was compiled by French weekly L’Express, which interviewed 60 serving and former intelligence officers from 25 intelligence organisations. Sixteen of those interviewed had served as current or former heads of an intelligence agency, according to Ynet. The services were assessed on their ability to recruit and develop agents, penetrate centres of political and institutional power, conduct covert operations and sabotage, and carry out cyber operations. MI6 received the highest overall assessment, particularly for its reported ability to recruit and cultivate long-term human sources in countries including Russia, China, Iran and Turkey. One French intelligence official told L’Express that Britain sometimes recruits individuals from elite universities years before activating them as intelligence sources. The French DGSE ranked second, with respondents highlighting its global reach and its ability to combine human intelligence with covert and technical operations. A Polish intelligence officer described France as one of the few European countries capable of conducting sensitive operations without attracting public attention. Five participants placed the French service at the top of their rankings. The Netherlands ranked third, a result that L’Express described as surprising. The Dutch intelligence community has played a significant role in major European cyber operations and has been linked in previous reports to efforts surrounding the Stuxnet malware operation targeting Iran’s nuclear programme. The Netherlands has not publicly acknowledged responsibility for such an operation. Germany ranked fifth, with one US intelligence source quoted by L’Express criticising the country’s intelligence service as overly bureaucratic and more focused on analysis than operational activity. Ukraine also received strong praise from European intelligence officials for the rapid transformation of its intelligence services during the war with Russia. Officials highlighted Ukrainian operations that they described as increasingly sophisticated, unconventional and effective. Some European officers reportedly compared this transformation to the development of Israel’s Mossad. Intelligence services in Scandinavia and the Baltic states were also rated highly, particularly because of their experience countering Russian espionage, influence operations and other forms of intelligence activity. Israel was not formally included in the European ranking, although former Mossad chief Yossi Cohen participated in the survey. Étienne Girard, deputy editor of L’Express, said in a personal assessment that a global ranking would likely place the United States first, with Mossad potentially ranking second or third behind Britain. The survey does not represent an official assessment of intelligence capabilities and is based on the views of a relatively small group of current and former intelligence officials. Its findings nevertheless offer an unusual inside perspective on how European intelligence professionals assess their counterparts across human intelligence, covert operations and cyber capabilities.
